verdict.rationale: Twilio documents an Authy API, with SDKs for common web languages, for integrating Authy two-factor authentication into apps. However, Twilio's own docs say the Authy API is closed to new customers and will be fully deprecated, so a new AI-native user cannot build on it. Verify is a separate successor product and earns no credit here. Missing for 10: an API open to new users, any API for driving the end-user authenticator app itself (tokens, devices, backups), endpoint reference depth, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: So you don't have to use the Authy API directly to integrate two-factor authentication into your app, we provide an SDK for common web languages.
The Authy API is now closed to new customers and will be fully deprecated in the future.
